moves.headline: Dollar Tree jumps 11% as traffic accelerates and it raises its earnings outlook
moves.summary: Dollar Tree rose 11.2% to $154.65 after third-quarter comparable sales grew 4.6%, above its own range, with traffic up 3.8%. It raised its full-year adjusted earnings outlook to $8.05–$8.25 a share, a figure that includes about $0.65 of tariff refunds.
why: Total revenue rose 6.9% to $5.1 billion, and traffic growth of 3.8% showed that its move to sell items above $1.25 in about 7,400 multi-price stores is drawing more shoppers. Margins fell because the company is reinvesting tariff refunds in prices and stores, but investors focused on the sales momentum and the higher guidance.

The move also benefited from a rotation on November 24 out of chip stocks and into retailers, consumer staples and health care: Dick’s Sporting Goods rose about 15% the same day on its own strong results.
context: On November 24 the Nasdaq fell about 1.5% and the S&P 500 about 0.5% while the Dow rose almost 0.9%, as chip stocks gave back much of the previous day’s rally after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang. Nvidia fell about 6–7% and AMD, Micron and Broadcom also dropped.
Money rotated out of semiconductors and AI hardware into health care, consumer staples and retailers, so most stocks rose even as the technology-heavy indexes fell.

src.title: Dow rises, S&P 500 and Nasdaq decline as chip sector tumbles (Yahoo Finance)
